validity.researcher_notes: GEOGRAPHY ERROR, carried on BOTH twin rows (not unique to P5121 -- checked P0530, same defect). Ain Sukhna (the pipeline's start terminal) is on the WEST shore of the Gulf of Suez, in Suez Governorate, mainland Egypt -- English Wikipedia's 'Ain Sokhna' article infobox gives Governorate = Suez, coordinates 29.6N 32.3167E. The Sinai Peninsula lies on the EAST side of the Gulf of Suez / Suez Canal; Ain Sukhna is not part of it and no source calls it Sinai. GEM's 'StartPrefecture/District: Sinai Peninsula' on P5121 (and P0530) is geographically wrong. Separately, the two twin rows also disagree with each other on 'StartState/Province' ('Suez Gulf' on P5121 vs 'North Red Sea' on P0530) for what should be the identical physical terminal -- an internal inconsistency worth reconciling at the same time. validity.researcher_notes: GEM's FuelSource = 'Gulf of Suez' appears to conflate the pipeline's START LOCATION's geographic feature (the terminal sits on the Gulf of Suez) with the actual origin of the oil it carries, which is a different body of water entirely. Both independent sources that describe the pipeline's purpose are explicit that the crude comes from the Persian/Arabian Gulf, not from Egypt's own (much smaller) Gulf of Suez oil fields: English Wikipedia -- 'It provides an alternative to the Suez Canal for transporting oil from the Persian Gulf region to the Mediterranean'; Al Jazeera/Bloomberg (2020) -- 'the Sumed transports Middle Eastern oil to the North African coast' and 'Egypt's Sumed pipeline was designed to pump 2.5 million barrels of Persian Gulf crude from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean every day.' SUMED exists precisely because VLCCs too large for the Suez Canal offload Persian Gulf crude at Ain Sukhna, which the pipeline then carries to the Mediterranean for reloading -- the fuel source is Persian Gulf crude, not locally produced Gulf of Suez crude. Same defect on P0530 (checked). Not staging a replacement value/ref here (wrong-value correction is an Update-leg edit, not a ref-only fill).

fills.researcher_notes: Status inferred from context, not a literal token match (per verifier guidance): a July 2020 news account of real, tanker-tracked barrel flows through the pipeline confirms it is an active, operating asset.

Per-line figure is a DERIVED value, not a value either source states directly: both sources give the AGGREGATE two-line design capacity as 2.5 million bpd (Wikipedia infobox 'Maximum discharge 2.5 million barrels per day'; Al Jazeera/Bloomberg 'designed to pump 2.5 million barrels ... every day'). 2,500,000 / 2 lines = 1,250,000 bpd matches GEM's per-line value exactly, but since no source states 1,250,000 for a single line explicitly, tier is medium rather than high.

UN ESCWA's terminology database gives the Arabic name 'الشركة العربية لأنابيب البترول' with acronym '(سوميد)' -- an EXACT character-for-character match to GEM's Operator string. English Wikipedia independently names 'Arab Petroleum Pipeline Company (Sumed Company)' as operator. Two independent origins (a UN body vs. an encyclopedia), same entity.

Both sources confirm the JV company (SUMED / Arab Petroleum Pipelines Co) is the entity that owns and operates the physical pipeline asset, supporting Owner1 = 100%. Tier held at medium rather than high because neither source states the underlying shareholder split (Wikipedia: EGPC 50%, Saudi Aramco 15%, IPIC 15%, three Kuwaiti companies 5% each, QatarEnergy 5%; ESCWA lists EGPC, the Saudi oil company, three Kuwaiti companies and Qatar Petroleum as the JV partners but omits IPIC/UAE entirely) -- worth a researcher's-notes flag that GEM's single 100%-owner model does not surface the underlying multi-government shareholding, and that the two sources' own partner lists don't fully agree with each other on the shareholder roster.

summary: P5121 (Sumed Oil Pipeline, Pipeline 2) is a real, well-documented physical line -- confirmed high-tier via Wikipedia + Al Jazeera/Bloomberg + UN ESCWA -- and its near-identical pairing with P0530 is CONFIRMED as SUMED's two genuine parallel 42-inch/320 km lines, not a duplicate. Two attribution defects found (shared with P0530): StartPrefecture/District 'Sinai Peninsula' is geographically wrong (Ain Sukhna is Suez Governorate, west of the Gulf of Suez), and FuelSource 'Gulf of Suez' misstates the oil's origin (sources say Persian Gulf crude). ProposalYear 1974 is an open, low-confidence question -- sources disagree with each other on a 1973-vs-1977 founding chronology. 8 refs staged (Fuel, Status, Start, Length, Diameter, Capacity, EndLocation, Operator, Owner all REFS_ADDED); none UNRESOLVED.
